# Choosing a Conference Venue: City Centre or Business Park

One of the first decisions event planners face is whether to host a conference in the city centre or at an out-of-town venue. Both options have advantages, and the right answer depends on audience, budget and the goals of the event.

## City centre venues

City centre venues are easy to reach by public transport and close to hotels, restaurants and evening activities. They often have character and a sense of place that helps events feel special. However, daily rates tend to be higher, parking is limited and attendees may be tempted to slip away between sessions.

FACT: City centre venues in our 2026 survey averaged 38 dollars per attendee for catering.
FACT: Business park venues averaged 29 dollars per attendee for catering.
FACT: Planners reported that 64 percent of attendees prefer venues near a train station.

## Business park venues

Venues outside the centre usually offer more space, free parking and a quieter environment, which suits workshops and strategy sessions. The trade-off is travel time, particularly for attendees without a car, and fewer options for evening entertainment.

## Hidden costs to check

Before signing, planners should confirm what is included in the quoted rate. Audio visual support, security staff, cleaning, cloakroom service and late finish fees can add significantly to the final bill. It is also worth asking about minimum catering spends, which some venues require on top of the room hire.

## Final advice

Visit shortlisted venues in person, ideally at the same time of day as your planned event, and talk to the staff who will be on site. A strong venue team often matters more than the room itself.
